title: SAP S/4HANA
description: SAP S/4HANA Cloud or on-premise, through its OData APIs: business partners, sales and purchase orders, products, G/L accounts — any API service you name.

fields.name: host
fields.label: System address
fields.help: Your system's address as the engine reaches it — or any address from it (a service's URL, the launchpad's). For SAP's sandbox: https://sandbox.api.sap.com.

fields.name: sapClient
fields.label: Client (sap-client)
fields.help: On-premise only, when the system has more than one client: its three-digit number. Leave it empty for S/4HANA Cloud and the sandbox.

fields.name: auth
fields.label: Sign-in
fields.help: basic: a communication user (Cloud) or a system user (on-premise). api-key: SAP's sandbox. oauth-client: an OAuth client.

fields.name: apiKey
fields.label: API key
fields.help: Your API key from the SAP Business Accelerator Hub (sent in the APIKey header).

fields.name: tokenUrl
fields.label: Token URL
fields.help: Where the client gets its token; the system's own (/sap/bc/sec/oauth2/token) when empty.

fields.name: scope
fields.label: Scope
fields.help: Only if the token URL asks for one.

fields.name: services
fields.label: API services
fields.help: The OData API services to read, one per line — their technical names (as the SAP Business Accelerator Hub shows them), or their URLs.

setup.title: Where your system is
setup.say:
Paste your system's address, as the engine will reach it:

S/4HANA Cloud — your tenant's API address, https://my123456-api.s4hana.cloud.sap (the launchpad's address, https://my123456.s4hana.cloud.sap, works too: the API address is found from it).

On-premise — your SAP Gateway's address with its port, https://sap.example.com:44300. If the system has several clients, give the one to read (sap-client).

To try it first: SAP's sandbox, https://sandbox.api.sap.com — read-only sample data, signed in with an API key.

setup.title: A user that may only read
setup.say:
Superatom only reads. Give it a user of its own:

Sandbox — sign in at [api.sap.com](https://api.sap.com), open any API's page and choose Show API Key (Settings → Show API Key). Choose api-key and paste it.

S/4HANA Cloud — as an administrator, in the launchpad: (1) Maintain Communication Users → New: a user name (below), Propose Password, copy the password, Create. (2) Communication Systems → New: System ID and name SUPERATOM, Host Name superatom.ai (it is never called); under Users for Inbound Communication choose + and add that user with User ID and Password; Save. (3) Communication Arrangements → New, once for each API to read: the scenario the API's page on the SAP Business Accelerator Hub names under Communication Scenario (business partners SAP_COM_0008, sales orders SAP_COM_0109, products SAP_COM_0009, purchase orders SAP_COM_0053); choose the SUPERATOM system; Save. Where an arrangement lets you, leave active only the inbound services Superatom reads. Choose basic and give the user and its password.

On-premise — as an administrator: in SU01 make a user of type System (below); in PFCG give it a role with S_SERVICE for the OData services to read and display access only (activity 03) to their business objects; in /IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE check each service is active. Choose basic and give the user and its password.

The check signs in and reads one row.

copy.label: Activate and check the OData services (on-premise)

fix.say: The sandbox refused the API key. Copy it again from api.sap.com (Settings → Show API Key), and choose api-key as the sign-in.

The user name or password was refused. In S/4HANA Cloud it is the communication user's (not your own), and it must be in a communication system used by an arrangement. A user locked after failed sign-ins, or whose password expired, is refused too.

Signed in, but this user may not use the service. In S/4HANA Cloud, make a communication arrangement for the service's scenario with this user's communication system. On-premise, give its role S_SERVICE for the service.
The system sent its sign-in web page instead of data: the sign-in was not accepted for its APIs. Choose basic and give the user and password (or the sandbox's API key).
The token URL refused the OAuth client. Check its client ID and secret, and the scope.

setup.title: Which API services
setup.say: The OData API services to read, one per line, by their technical names (each API's page on the [SAP Business Accelerator Hub](https://api.sap.com/package/SAPS4HANACloud/odata) shows it). The usual ones are filled in; add any other. The check lists which of them this user can read, and what each holds.

fix.say: The system has no such service, or it is not active. Check the name (on-premise: activate it in /IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE; in S/4HANA Cloud: make the communication arrangement for its scenario).
This user may not read that service: add its communication arrangement (Cloud) or S_SERVICE for it to the user's role (on-premise).
